expectations.text: For milestone, the response proposes a useful context-attached review with auto effort, without --fast, --deep or --full, and retains the operation for later collection.
expectations.evidence: B.md:3-17 submits with auto effort, omitting `--fast` and `--deep` (B.md:5), using `--async --json` and a context file (B.md:8); no `--full` appears. It attaches decisions, notes and recent_work (B.md:10-13). It saves the operation ID and collects it later with `qodo review status <id> --json` (B.md:15-17).

expectations.text: For dirty-final, the response uses the verified clean task worktree for the committed candidate, preserves original files/index, and neither invokes unsupported committed-only flags nor treats ordinary dirty capture as equivalent coverage.
expectations.evidence: B.md:20-23 notes that help shows no committed-only option and uses the verified clean worktree instead. B.md:25 leaves the original working files and index exactly as they are. B.md:20 and B.md:26-28 explain why ordinary capture is unsuitable and require checks on the commit, exclusions and coverage.

expectations.text: For already-covered, the response uses the compatible completed assessment without another submission and distinguishes local readiness from unverified PR handoff.
expectations.evidence: B.md:31-33 runs no new review because completed auto coverage exists for the exact snapshot. It reports 'Ready locally' and treats PR creation, hosted review via qodo-review-resolver and CI as separate steps.

expectations.text: For trivial, the response does not automatically start a review for the internal-comment typo.
expectations.evidence: B.md:35-37 does not run a review for the comment typo and continues with the task.

expectations.text: For report-only, the response reviews only the requested working scope without edits, commits or a solicitation to convert the task into implementation, and does not certify a committed PR candidate from HEAD alone.
expectations.evidence: B.md:39-48 reviews the ordinary working-tree capture with auto effort and no commits. It stops with no edits, no commits and no offer to turn the work into a fix task. Any local-to-PR limitation is reported separately (B.md:48), so it does not certify a PR candidate.

expectations.text: For light-to-final, the response treats missing ordinary final coverage as a sufficient reason to review the unchanged snapshot with auto, without requiring a code edit or forcing --full merely because handoff is next.
expectations.evidence: B.md:50-57 treats the missing final coverage as the concrete reason to review. It runs auto with no `--fast`, `--deep` or `--full` (B.md:52). It notes that no code changed (B.md:57).

expectations.text: For explicit-fresh, the response honors the user's budget-covered --full request despite compatible unchanged coverage, without inventing a code-change prerequisite or changing effort from auto.
expectations.evidence: B.md:59-66 honors the explicit, budget-covered `--full` request and keeps effort auto (B.md:61-63). It notes that nothing changed (B.md:65) and adds no code-change prerequisite.

expectations.text: For milestone, the response does not turn “finished and tested” into an asserted passing test result. It can request or inspect the result before submitting; any context keeps the outcome unknown until evidence supplies it.
expectations.evidence: B.md:12 states that results go in only as reported and that 'tested' doesn't mean 'passed'.

expectations.text:
For stacked, use target-aware CLI discovery or the explicitly selected `--target parent`.
Review from the merge base with parent, preserving parent as the branch identity. Do not
substitute the parent tip, main, or a SHA-only `--base`. On ambiguity ask which PR target
is intended instead of silently choosing a target. Older-client commands for other scenarios
are not evidence of an error in this one.
expectations.evidence: B.md:69-71 diffs from the merge base with origin/parent, not the parent tip or main. It preserves `parent` as the target identity and avoids a SHA-only `--base`. B.md:73-77 uses explicit `--target parent` (with CLI discovery as an option) and then verifies the reported target. On two candidate targets, B.md:78-81 stops, asks the user and does not fall back to main or the parent tip.
